evidence: src/domain/entities/Project.ts: static create(id, name) { const trimmed = name.trim(); if (trimmed.length === 0) throw new ValidationError('Project name must not be empty'); ... }

src/domain/entities/User.ts: static create(id, name) { const trimmed = name.trim(); if (trimmed.length === 0) throw new ValidationError('User name must not be empty'); ... }. This matches the check in Project.ts.

src/domain/entities/Task.ts: readonly title: TaskTitle; dueDate: DueDate; currentStatus: TaskStatus. Task delegates validation to value objects, while Project and User use a raw `readonly name: string`.
src/domain/entities/Task.ts: props.description.trim() is normalized inline in create rather than in a value object.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The three files fit together as one concern: domain entity classes, each with a private constructor and a static `create` factory. The rubric also requires each invariant to live in one place and the module's abstractions to be used consistently, and two problems break that.

1. The same rule is copied. `Project.create` and `User.create` contain an identical inline check: trim the name, throw `ValidationError` if it is empty, then construct the object. Only the message text differs.

2. The abstraction is used inconsistently. `Task` keeps its title validation inside the `TaskTitle` value object and types its fields with value objects (`TaskTitle`, `DueDate`, `TaskStatus`). `Project` and `User` instead hold raw `string` names and check them inline. Elsewhere in the same module, this invariant lives in a value object.

`Task` also trims `description` inline in `create`, which is a smaller instance of the same habit.

The duplication is small, and project names and user names are arguably different concepts. That is why confidence is only moderate. Even so, the rubric's duplication and consistency conditions are met.

violations.message: Project.create repeats the same trim-and-not-empty name check found in User.create. It holds `name` as a raw string, while Task uses a value object (TaskTitle) for this kind of validation. The shared name rule should live in one place, such as a value object.
User.create copies the trim-and-not-empty name check from Project.create, and it doesn't use the value-object pattern that Task uses for TaskTitle.
